title: The real wrapper composition supplies designBrief, so compiler and node missions carry the goal's design (or its declared skip)
description: Filed by the governor 20:22Z from worker-f78e0703's read-only roll-up of the design parent (task-8a6d6660, comment-f95b0ac3, anchor f213b41d). definitionOfDone: agent-wrapper-main.ts's createAgentWrapper supplies `designBrief`: it resolves the goal's durable design state through the existing design read (PRESENT with entities/ref/screens, SKIPPED with the operator's declaration, ABSENT only when truly absent) for the step's goal - unreadable state is a refusal with code + layer, never collapsed into ABSENT.

The node/compiler design provenance is the design VERSION the plan was built on (task-f3409f9a's fold), not 'latest': a goal with two design versions yields the planned one in the mission bytes; asserted.

Composed-mission tests through the REAL wrapper composition (not a hand-built brief): PRESENT emits the design paragraph naming at least one real entity; SKIPPED emits the skip words and never the 'NO DESIGN ACCOMPANIES' sentence; ABSENT keeps today's sentence. Assert the actual mission bytes.
A live-ish trace: on a store with a submitted design (fixture-free), the compiler mission a real seat would receive contains the design ref; recorded in a row comment with the command used.

Fresh focused daemon tests (agent-mission-text, agent-wrapper, agent-wrapper-main and the new composition arm) + `pnpm typecheck` EXIT 0 with a planted-error control; broader gates per lease rules; paths declared; parent task-8a6d6660's DoD 2 and its trace/skip clauses become certifiable from this row's evidence.

implementationPlan.description: THE RESOLVER, in a new module `apps/daemon/src/orchestrator/wrapper-mission-inputs.ts`. Export `createDesignBriefResolver({store, projectId, compiled})` returning `(kind, target) => DesignBrief | null`, matching `AgentWrapperConfig.designBrief`'s signature exactly. Resolve the step's GOAL first: for a COMPILER step `target` IS the goalId; for a node step `target` is a nodeRef, so map it by calling `activeCompiledGraphs(store, projectId)` and `compiledExecutionRef(projectId, graph, nodeKey)` — the SAME two exported functions `sealedNodesOf` uses — and never by re-deriving the ref by hand. An unresolvable nodeRef returns `null`, which `nodeDesignLines` already documents as "the caller knows nothing"; that is the ONE legitimate null and it is not a collapse. THE TWO LANES READ DIFFERENTLY, and this is the plan's central decision: a COMPILER seat is staffed BEFORE a plan exists, so there is no compiled binding and it reads LATEST (call `readDesignRevision` with NO `planningRunRef`); a NODE seat is staffed after, so it reads the PLANNED version (pass `planningRunRef: refsOfGoal(goalId).planningRunRef`). SKIPPED with the operator's reason : PRESENT with `ref` = `${goalRef}@v${record.version}`, `screens` = the flattened `screen` names of every journey (deduped, order preserved), `entities` = the `entity` names; `DESIGN_REVISION_ABSENT` -> ABSENT; EVERY OTHER CODE (`DESIGN_RECORD_MALFORMED`, store failures) -> UNREADABLE carrying that code and its layer. `!ok -> ABSENT` is the exact collapse DoD 1 forbids and must not appear.

implementationPlan.note:
STEP 5 — 9 ARMS, ALL THROUGH THE REAL COMPOSITION. `Test Files  1 passed (1)`, `Tests  9 passed (9)`, EXIT 0.

NOT ONE ARM BUILDS A BRIEF BY HAND. Every arm constructs a real `SqliteEventStore` (`boundWorld` -> `committedRevision` -> `approveGate1` from `plan-reject-test-fixtures.ts`), submits design records through PRODUCTION `submitDesignRevision`, calls `createDesignBriefResolver(...)` exactly as `agent-wrapper.ts:289/302` does, and asserts THE MISSION BYTES `codeMission`/`compilerMission` return. That is the distinction DoD 3 names: `agent-mission-text.test.ts` had 42 green arms while no production caller supplied `designBrief` at all.

THE ARMS
1. PRESENT/compiler — `A DESIGN EXISTS for this goal, submitted under design ref "goal-...@v1"`, and NOT `NO DESIGN ACCOMPANIES`.
2. PRESENT/node — names REAL entities and screens READ OFF the stored record (`revision.dataModel[0].entity`, `revision.screens[0].screens[0].screen`, pinned `toBe("User")`), not retyped literals, so a fixture edit cannot leave it green while citing a name the design no longer draws.
3. SKIPPED — the skip sentence WITH the operator's exact reason, and NOT `NO DESIGN ACCOMPANIES`.
4. ABSENT — today's sentence verbatim, and neither `A DESIGN EXISTS` nor `COULD NOT BE READ`.
5. UNREADABLE/compiler — a Proxy that throws ONLY for `design:<goal>` (every other read still works, so the arm measures the design path, not a broken store): bytes carry `DESIGN_STORE_UNAVAILABLE`, `answered by the LEDGER layer`, `THAT IS A FAILED READ, NOT A GOAL WITHOUT A DESIGN`, and NOT `NO DESIGN ACCOMPANIES`.
6. UNREADABLE/node — a sealed body under a run ref that bound nothing: `DESIGN_RECORD_MALFORMED` + `LEDGER` + "UNREADABLE rather than missing", and NOT the node ABSENT sentence.
7. **DoD 2, PROVENANCE** — design v1, compile+approve, THEN design v2. Node mission contains `@v1`, NOT `@v2`, and NOT `Session` (the entity only v2 adds). The same store's compiler mission contains `@v2`. Latest and planned are asserted in ONE arm, so neither can be satisfied by accident.
8. nodeRef -> goal through `activeCompiledGraphs` — the real sealed ref resolves to `{outcome: PRESENT, ref: goal@v1}`; an unknown ref answers null and produces bytes with no design paragraph.
